newsitem.title: USA: CBOT NEW CROP SOYBEANS UP SHARPLY ON DRIER OUTLOOK.
newsitem.headline: CBOT NEW CROP SOYBEANS UP SHARPLY ON DRIER OUTLOOK.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures were up sharply on Wednesday as some meteorologists reduced rainfall amounts and coverage in their weekend weather forecasts, traders said.

"There is rain in the forecast but the question is how much," a trader said. "Several of the forecasters think that the rain is going to be centered more to the north and we need it in the central and southern areas."

Weather Services Corp said Wednesday that rains of 0.25 to 1.00 inch were likely on Sunday or Monday with coverage of 40 to 60 percent. But WSC senior agricultural meteorologist David Taylor said the rains may be lightest in the areas where corn and soybean crops most need moisture.
Traders also noted soybeans had fallen sharply earlier this week on wetter weather outlooks and were due for a bounce.
At 1040 CDT, soybeans were up 13-1/2 to five cents per bushel with November up 13-1/2 at $6.48 per bushel.
